note: VibeCode QA standards registry. Maps a repo or slice detectable signals to the published or planned standards it should be judged against. Consumers: the vcqa CLI/engine, deterministic resolvers, and AI judges that must use fixed standards instead of memory. See SCHEMA.md.

signals.note: Reference of the atoms a `detect` predicate may test, gathered per slice or repo by the resolver.
signals.dep: a dependency name present in package.json (deps + devDeps) or pubspec.yaml (dependencies + dev_dependencies)
signals.file: an exact file present in the slice
signals.fileGlob: a glob matched within the slice
signals.config: a parsed key present (e.g. wrangler.toml has [[d1_databases]], pubspec.yaml, firebase.json, melos.yaml)

standards.title: Node CLI Internal Tool

standards.maturityNote: Twelve candidate rules carry severity, evidence, and exception terms, and `ref-node-cli-internal-tool` is published with a self-reported score and a green CI run. Blocking v1: no independent assessment of the reference repo exists, and the exit-code and JSON-mode rules have no scanner signal yet.

standards.title: TypeScript SDK

standards.maturityNote: Twelve candidate rules carry severity, evidence, and exception terms, and `ref-typescript-sdk` now exists, is published in the catalog, and carries a self-reported score with a green CI run ([#14](https://github.com/vibecodeqa/vibecodeqa/issues/14)). Blocking v1: the reference repo's report evidences the required implementation but does not judge R-SDK-1 to R-SDK-12 one by one at a named commit, and no independent assessment of the repo exists.

standards.title: GitHub Action Package
standards.summary: A packaged GitHub Action with action metadata, minimum permissions, validated inputs, pinned runtime/dependencies, and release tag policy.
standards.maturityNote: Matured from a backlog note on 2026-08-09 ([#37](https://github.com/vibecodeqa/vibecodeqa/issues/37)): candidate rules, upstream references, severity, exception policy, and CI evidence are on the page, and `ref-github-action-package` is now published in the catalog with a self-reported score, a green CI run, and a hand-argued R-GHA-1 to R-GHA-10 mapping ([#44](https://github.com/vibecodeqa/vibecodeqa/issues/44)). Blocking v1: that mapping is prose rather than a scanner signal, no independent assessment of the repo exists, no release tag has been cut so R-GHA-8 is documented but never exercised, and the composite and Docker runtimes are still unseparated from the JavaScript rules.

standards.title: VS Code Extension Package
standards.summary: A VS Code extension package with activation scope, workspace trust behavior, command/webview boundaries, marketplace metadata, and extension tests.
standards.maturityNote: Demoted on 2026-08-09 ([#37](https://github.com/vibecodeqa/vibecodeqa/issues/37)) because the only consumer the charter cited, `vibecodeqa/vscode`, was archived on 2026-07-23 without ever being published. A reference repo has since been built and is cataloged as experimental ([#19](https://github.com/vibecodeqa/vibecodeqa/issues/19)), which is why the demotion reason no longer stands alone. Detection was repaired on 2026-08-11 ([#47](https://github.com/vibecodeqa/vibecodeqa/issues/47)): the archetype now matches on `engines.vscode` or `contributes`, so the gap report a backlog entry exists to produce finally names this standard instead of `typescript-sdk`. Still blocking any promotion: this page carries no numbered candidate rules, no severity or exception policy, and no rubric can be cut from it. The page stays published so its URL keeps resolving.

standards.title: Tauri React Desktop
standards.summary: A Tauri desktop application with a React frontend, command/capability boundaries, secure storage posture, packaging, and typed frontend/backend contracts.
standards.maturityNote: Scope, composition, detection signals, and rule surface are recorded, but no numbered candidate rules exist, so nothing here is judgeable yet. `vibecodeqa/app` is a live in-house consumer, and `ref-tauri-react-desktop` is now built and cataloged as experimental with a self-reported score and a green CI run ([#21](https://github.com/vibecodeqa/vibecodeqa/issues/21)). Blocking a candidate rubric: the rule surface has to become numbered rules with severity, evidence, and an exception policy before either repo can be judged against it.

This repository's own docs site is the in-house consumer, and `ref-zensical-kb-site` is now built and cataloged as experimental with a self-reported score and a green CI run ([#17](https://github.com/vibecodeqa/vibecodeqa/issues/17)). Blocking a candidate rubric: the rule surface has to become numbered rules with severity, evidence, and an exception policy, and the reference repo's KB-quality model is the obvious input for authoring them.
